transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um... I guess I'm just having some trouble at work lately. I've been... well, I keep getting up during these long sales strategy meetings we have. I know I'm supposed to just stay seated, but I find myself finding excuses to leave... like getting up to refill my water, or just pacing by the printer. It's becoming an issue.
Have you started or changed any medications recently, such as antipsychotics, anti-nausea drugs, or other prescriptions, before this restlessness began?
Um... no. I haven't started anything new. I don't really take any medications like that.

When you feel the urge to get up and pace during these meetings, is it linked to feeling anxious, worried, or fearful about something specific, or does it just feel like a general restlessness you can't control?
Um... no, I don't think I'm worried about anything specific. It's not like I'm anxious or afraid... I just... I don't know, I just get restless. I just feel like I need to move.
Have you noticed this kind of restlessness or trouble staying still going back to childhood or your teenage years, or is this something that's really only started recently?

Um... yeah, it goes back a long way. I think it started way before high school. I remember... well, my elementary school teachers used to write notes about it. They'd say I was smart but that I rushed through things. And, um, I guess I talked out of turn a lot. I always forgot my homework, too. My desk was always just... stuffed with half-finished papers. So, yeah, it's not new.

Have you ever had a distinct period of several days or more where you felt unusually elevated, euphoric, or irritable, and needed much less sleep than usual, that was different from how you normally feel?
Um... no. I haven't really had anything like that. I just... I sleep normally, mostly. I haven't had any days where I felt like that.
Besides at work, do you notice this restlessness, trouble focusing, or disorganization affecting you in other areas of your life, like at home or in social situations?

Um... I'm not really sure about home. It's mostly just... work. That's where I notice it. It's, um, it's started showing up in my performance reviews lately. And... well, there was a client complaint recently about it. I don't really want to get into the details, but... it just made me worry that I might damage my accounts. I do care a lot about doing a good job, it's just... yeah. Mostly work.
Thinking specifically about your home life or relationships with family and friends, have people close to you ever mentioned that you seem restless, forgetful, or disorganized in those settings?
Um... no. Not really. I don't really talk about that kind of stuff with them. We just... hang out, I guess. Nobody's really said anything like that to me.
Can you think of a specific time recently—like during a movie, a meal with friends, or doing chores at home—when you found it hard to sit still or stay focused, even if no one commented on it?

Um... I don't know. Not really. I can't really think of a specific time. I just... I don't really pay attention to that kind of thing outside of the office. Like I said, it's pretty much just work where I notice it being an issue.
Do you ever have trouble keeping up with personal tasks like paying bills on time, keeping appointments, or managing household chores?
Um... no, not really. I mean, my bills are on autopay, so... that's fine. And I guess I keep up with chores okay. It's just... normal stuff. I don't really have a problem with it.
Do you often lose track of personal items, like your keys or wallet, or make careless mistakes in everyday tasks outside of work?

No, I don't think so. I usually just leave my keys in the same spot by the door, so... I don't really lose them. And I don't really know what you mean by careless mistakes. I just do what I need to do.
Do you often find yourself interrupting conversations, blurting out answers before someone finishes a question, or having difficulty waiting your turn in discussions?

Um... yeah, I guess that happens sometimes. Mostly at work. I'll... I'll jump in with an answer before a client or a coworker is done asking something. And then... I realize I answered the wrong thing or, you know, just cut them off. So... yeah, I do that.
